T: Wings out, napkins on. The schnitzel lands first.
D: An eccentric inventor rebuilds an old racing car for his two children, and it carries them, their father and a new friend to a kingdom where children are forbidden.
P: Serve the snacks when Caractacus switches on his breakfast machine and it starts cooking on its own.
S: Caractacus's breakfast machine boiling the eggs and frying the sausages on its own

Soft-centred boiled eggs wrapped in parsley and mustard sausage meat, crumbed and fried golden, with English mustard. Boil 4 eggs for 6 1/2 minutes, cool in iced water and peel. Mix 400g pork sausage mince with 2 tbsp chopped parsley, 1 tsp mustard powder and pepper, divide into 4 and flatten each on wet hands. Wrap around the eggs and seal well. Roll in 50g plain flour, then 1 beaten egg, then 80g dry breadcrumbs, and chill for 20 minutes. Heat 1 litre of oil to 170C and fry 2 at a time for about 7 minutes, turning, until deep golden. Drain, halve and serve warm with English mustard.
the beach picnic with the two children and their new friend

Crustless white bread fingers with thin salted cucumber and lemon and dill cream cheese. Toss 1 very thinly sliced telegraph cucumber with 1/2 tsp salt and drain for 15 minutes. Beat 125g soft cream cheese with 40g soft butter, 1 tbsp chopped dill, the zest of 1 lemon and a little white pepper. Spread over 8 slices of white bread, pat the cucumber dry and layer it over 4 slices, then close. Cut off the crusts and cut each sandwich into 3 fingers.
M: the Baron's birthday banquet, stormed by the children

Thin crumbed pork schnitzel fried golden in butter, with lemon and a warm mustard and chive potato salad. Boil 800g kipfler potatoes until tender. Warm 125ml vegetable stock with 2 tbsp white wine vinegar, 1 tsp Dijon mustard and 1 finely chopped small red onion, slice the potatoes hot, pour over the dressing, add 3 tbsp oil and chopped chives and season. Pound 600g pork loin steaks to 5mm between baking paper and season. Dip in 75g plain flour, 2 beaten eggs and 150g dry breadcrumbs. Fry in 150ml oil and 30g butter over medium high heat for 2 to 3 minutes a side until golden. Serve with lemon wedges and the warm potato salad.
Lord Scrumptious's roast beef and Yorkshires
Truly's father, the sweet factory lord who buys the Toot Sweets for the dogs

Roast sirloin with Yorkshire puddings, roast potatoes, gravy and horseradish cream. Whisk 120g of the flour, the eggs, milk and a pinch of salt into a smooth batter and leave to stand. Heat the oven to 220C. Rub the beef with 1 tbsp of the oil and salt and roast for 45 minutes for medium rare, with the parboiled potatoes in 1 tbsp of oil on another tray. Rest the beef. Turn the oven to 230C, put a drop of the rest of the oil in a 12-hole muffin tin and heat for 5 minutes, fill with batter and bake for 18 minutes until puffed. Stir the rest of the flour into the beef pan, whisk in the stock and simmer for 4 minutes for gravy. Whip the cream softly and fold in the horseradish. Carve and serve with the Yorkshires, potatoes, gravy and horseradish cream.
W: the Toymaker's shop, where the Pottses hide as jack-in-the-boxes

Dark, sticky golden syrup gingerbread with ginger and cinnamon, cut in warm squares under hot vanilla custard. Heat the oven to 170C and line a 20cm square tin. Melt 125g butter, 125g brown sugar and 175g golden syrup together. Mix 250g plain flour, 2 tsp ground ginger, 1 tsp cinnamon and 1 tsp bicarbonate of soda, then whisk in the syrup mixture, 1 egg and 200ml milk. Pour into the tin and bake for 40 minutes until risen and springy. Warm 500ml vanilla custard and serve over warm squares of the gingerbread.
K: Jeremy and Jemima's lemon barley water
Jeremy and Jemima, who find the old racing car in the junkyard

Old-fashioned cloudy barley water with lemon zest and juice, lightly sweet and served icy with lemon slices. Rinse 100g pearl barley and simmer with 1.5 litres of water and the zest of 3 lemons for 30 minutes. Strain into a jug over 100g caster sugar and stir to dissolve, then cool and chill for 1 hour. Stir in the juice of the 3 lemons and serve over ice with lemon slices.

dishes.make_ahead: Wrap and crumb the eggs up to 1 day ahead and chill; fry on the day. Cooked, they keep 2 days in the fridge for a cold picnic

steps.text: Lower 4 eggs into boiling water for 6 1/2 minutes, then cool in iced water and peel.
Mix the sausage mince with the parsley, mustard powder and pepper, divide into 4 and flatten each into a patty on wet hands.
Wrap a patty around each egg, sealing it well.
Roll in the flour, then the beaten egg, then the breadcrumbs.
Chill for 20 minutes so they hold their shape. Heat the oil in a deep pan to 170C.
Fry 2 at a time, turning, until deep golden and cooked through, about 7 minutes.
Drain, halve and serve warm with the mustard.

dishes.make_ahead: Mix the dill cream cheese up to 2 days ahead; make the sandwiches up to 2 hours ahead, cover with a damp tea towel and chill

steps.text: Toss the cucumber with the salt in a colander and leave to drain.
Beat the cream cheese, butter, dill, lemon zest and a little white pepper until smooth.
Spread over the bread, pat the cucumber dry and layer it over 4 slices, then close the sandwiches.
Cut off the crusts and cut each sandwich into 3 fingers.

dishes.make_ahead: Make the potato salad up to 4 hours ahead and keep at room temperature; crumb the schnitzels up to 4 hours ahead and chill; fry to serve

steps.text: Boil the potatoes in salted water until tender.
Warm the stock with the vinegar, mustard and onion. Slice the potatoes while hot, pour the dressing over, add the oil and chives, season and leave to soak.
Pound the pork between sheets of baking paper to 5mm thin and season.
Dip each in flour, then egg, then breadcrumbs, pressing them on.
Fry in the oil and butter over medium high heat, 2 to 3 minutes a side, in batches, until golden and crisp.
Serve with lemon wedges and the warm potato salad.

veg.make_ahead: Make the potato salad up to 4 hours ahead and keep at room temperature; crumb the eggplant up to 2 hours ahead; fry to serve

steps.text: Boil the potatoes in salted water until tender.
Warm the stock with the vinegar, mustard and onion. Slice the potatoes while hot, pour the dressing over, add the oil and chives, season and leave to soak.
Salt the eggplant slices lightly, leave for 10 minutes, then pat dry.
Dip each in flour, then egg, then breadcrumbs, pressing them on.
Fry in the oil and butter over medium heat, 3 to 4 minutes a side, in batches, until golden and soft inside.
Serve with lemon wedges and the warm potato salad.

dishes.n: Lord Scrumptious's roast beef and Yorkshires
dishes.make_ahead: Make the Yorkshire batter up to 1 day ahead and keep in the fridge

steps.text: Whisk 120g of the flour, the eggs, milk and a pinch of salt into a smooth batter and leave to stand.
Heat the oven to 220C. Rub the beef with 1 tbsp of the oil and salt and roast for 45 minutes for medium rare, with the parboiled potatoes in 1 tbsp of oil on another tray.
Rest the beef. Turn the oven to 230C, put a drop of the rest of the oil in a 12-hole muffin tin and heat for 5 minutes, fill with batter and bake for 18 minutes until puffed.
Stir the rest of the flour into the beef pan, whisk in the stock and simmer for 4 minutes for gravy. Whip the cream softly and fold in the horseradish.
Carve and serve with the Yorkshires, potatoes, gravy and horseradish cream.

veg.n: Lord Scrumptious's mushroom Wellington and Yorkshires
veg.make_ahead: Make and wrap the Wellington up to 1 day ahead and chill

steps.text: Whisk 120g of the flour, 3 eggs, the milk and a pinch of salt into a smooth batter and leave to stand.
Fry the chopped mushrooms in 1 tbsp of the oil until dry, then wilt in the spinach. Cool, roll up in the pastry and brush with the last egg.
Bake at 220C for 35 minutes, with the parboiled potatoes in 1 tbsp of oil on another tray.
Put a drop of the rest of the oil in a 12-hole muffin tin and heat for 5 minutes, fill with batter and bake for 18 minutes until puffed.
Cook the rest of the flour in a little oil, whisk in the stock and simmer for 4 minutes for gravy. Whip the cream softly and fold in the horseradish.
Slice and serve with the Yorkshires, potatoes, gravy and horseradish cream.

dishes.make_ahead: Bake up to 3 days ahead and keep wrapped; it gets stickier. Warm through and heat the custard to serve

steps.text: Heat the oven to 170C and line a 20cm square tin.
Melt the butter, brown sugar and golden syrup together over low heat.
Mix the flour, ginger, cinnamon and bicarbonate of soda, then whisk in the syrup mixture, the egg and the milk to a smooth batter.
Pour into the tin and bake until risen and springy.
Warm the custard in a small pan.
Cut the gingerbread into squares and serve warm with the hot custard.

dishes.n: Jeremy and Jemima's lemon barley water
dishes.make_ahead: Make and chill up to 3 days ahead; stir in the lemon juice on the day

steps.text: Rinse the barley, then simmer it with the water and lemon zest for 30 minutes.
Strain into a jug over the sugar and stir until it dissolves.
Cool, then chill until cold.
Stir in the lemon juice and serve over ice with lemon slices.
